name: WE-039 Sorrel Basin Groundwater Allocation Plan (expand-loop blind run)

unclear.text: K4 allows transfers between wells in the Basin, subject to the Authority's rules on local impacts, and the hydrology chapter says impacts are managed by sub-basin: whether a share may be pumped outside the sub-basin of the parcel that earned it.
readings: U1-a: a share may be pumped only from a well in the sub-basin where the parcel that earned it lies
U1-b: a share may be pumped anywhere in the basin; the impact rules only set conditions on individual wells (spacing, monitoring)

a1.text: Without the cap, pumping would stay near 300,000 af and above 210,000.

a2.text: The cap is enforced against most pumpers: meters, telemetry and satellite checks detect most over-pumping.

a20.text: Landholders planning new orchards gave weight to the draft plan from 2022.

a22.text: Under U1-b, South growers could lease in enough North and Central allocations to approach South's counterfactual pumping.

a17.text: Some pumpers inflated 2017 to 2021 pumping in anticipation of allocation by history.

a27.text: Some landholders without history, including holders of parcels under 20 acres, would have started or expanded irrigation without the plan.

s1.text: Some domestic wells pump close to the 2 af a year line.
